what_its_for: Lorlatinib is a cancer medicine used to treat a type of lung cancer called non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). It works in patients whose cancer has a specific gene change called ALK-positive. It helps stop cancer cells from growing and spreading.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with or without food. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. If you vomit after taking a dose, do not take another dose that day — just take your next scheduled dose as usual.
dosing: The usual dose is 100 mg taken by mouth once a day. Your doctor may lower your dose or temporarily stop your medicine if you have side effects. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been less than 4 hours since your scheduled time, take it as soon as you remember. If more than 4 hours have passed, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store lorlatinib at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep it away from moisture, heat, and light. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicines down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a medicine take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it can increase the amount of drug in your body and cause more side effects. Avoid St. John's Wort supplements, as they can make lorlatinib less effective. Tell your doctor about ALL other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting, since many drugs can interact with lorlatinib. Do not drive or use heavy machinery if you feel confused, have memory problems, or feel dizzy, as this drug can affect your thinking and coordination.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: mood changes, confusion, memory problems, hallucinations, or unusual behavior (these may be signs of serious brain side effects); chest pain, shortness of breath, or swelling in your legs (possible heart or blood clot problems); high cholesterol or triglycerides noticed on blood tests; unusual swelling of the face, hands, or feet; high blood pressure; severe headache or vision changes; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain; or any new or worsening symptoms that worry you.
when_it_works: Lorlatinib starts working right away in your body, but it may take several weeks to months before you and your doctor notice changes in your cancer. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular scans and blood tests. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Lorlatinib can harm an unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for 6 months after the last dose. Male patients with female partners who can become pregnant should use effective contraception during treatment and for 3 months after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for 7 days after the last dose. Liver problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have moderate to severe liver disease. Kidney problems: Dose adjustments are generally not needed for kidney disease, but tell your doctor about any kidney problems. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects, especially those affecting thinking and mood — report any changes to your doctor promptly.
